# std/host.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from std/host.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

The command line, files and standard error, for
programs on the hosted target. Built on the `Host` capability, so a
kernel or user program that imports this file is rejected (`E-TARGET`).

`import "std/host.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`eprint_str`](#eprint_str) | Writes a literal to standard error. |
| [`eprint_text`](#eprint_text) | Writes a text built with core/text.bastio to standard error. |
| [`host_arg_is`](#host_arg_is) | Command-line argument `i` is the literal `s`. |
| [`read_file`](#read_file) | The whole file at `path`, if it can be read. |
| [`read_file_str`](#read_file_str) | `read_file` with the path given as a literal. |
| [`write_file_str`](#write_file_str) | Creates or replaces the file at `path`, given as a literal. |
| [`write_file`](#write_file) | Creates or replaces the file at `path`. |
| [`file_exists`](#file_exists) | The file at `path` can be read. |
| [`env_get`](#env_get) | The value of the environment variable `name`, if it is set. |
| [`host_args`](#host_args) | All command-line arguments, the program's own name first. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `eprint_str`

```bastio
fn eprint_str(h: &Host, s: Str)
```

Writes a literal to standard error.

Example:

```bastio
eprint_str(host, "warning: ");
let mut t = text_new();
text_push_str(&mut t, "nothing is wrong\n");
eprint_text(host, t);
vec_free(t);
```

### `eprint_text`

```bastio
fn eprint_text(h: &Host, t: &Vec[u8])
```

Writes a text built with core/text.bastio to standard error.

### `host_arg_is`

```bastio
fn host_arg_is(h: &Host, i: u64, s: Str) -> bool
```

Command-line argument `i` is the literal `s`.

Example:

```bastio
// Argument 0 is the program itself; no example is run with `--help`.
let asked = host_arg_is(host, 1, "--help");
if asked { return 1; }
```

### `read_file`

```bastio
fn read_file(h: &Host, path: &Bytes) -> Option[Bytes]
```

The whole file at `path`, if it can be read.

Example:

```bastio
// Read the running program's own file.
let me = host_arg(host, 0);
let mut n = 0;
match read_file(host, me) {
  Option::Some(b) => { n = blen(b); bfree(b); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(me);
let missing = read_file_str(host, "/nonexistent/bastio-example");
let mut ok = n > 0;
match missing {
  Option::Some(b) => { bfree(b); ok = false; },
  Option::None => {},
}
let data = bfrom("discarded");
ok = ok && write_file_str(host, "/dev/null", data);
bfree(data);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

```bastio
fn write_file_str(h: &Host, path: Str, data: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Creates or replaces the file at `path`, given as a literal.

### `write_file`

```bastio
fn write_file(h: &Host, path: &Bytes, data: &Bytes) -> bool
```

Creates or replaces the file at `path`.

Example:

```bastio
let p = bfrom("/dev/null");
let data = bfrom("discarded");
let ok = write_file(host, p, data);
bfree(data);
bfree(p);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `file_exists`

```bastio
fn file_exists(h: &Host, path: &Bytes) -> bool
```

The file at `path` can be read. The whole file is read to find out, so
this is for small files and for checking before a write, not for a path
that is a large file or a device.

Example:

```bastio
let me = host_arg(host, 0);
let there = file_exists(host, me);
bfree(me);
let nowhere = bfrom("/nonexistent/bastio-example");
let missing = file_exists(host, nowhere);
bfree(nowhere);
if !there || missing { return 1; }
```

### `env_get`

```bastio
fn env_get(h: &Host, name: Str) -> Option[Bytes]
```

The value of the environment variable `name`, if it is set.

Example:

```bastio
let mut ok = true;
match env_get(host, "BASTIO_SURELY_UNSET_VARIABLE") {
  Option::Some(v) => { bfree(v); ok = false; },
  Option::None => {},
}
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `host_args`

```bastio
fn host_args(h: &Host) -> Vec[Bytes]
```

All command-line arguments, the program's own name first. Free the result
with `bytes_vec_free`.

Example:

```bastio
let args = host_args(host);
let ok = vec_len(args) >= 1;
bytes_vec_free(args);
if !ok { return 1; }
```
